findings.title: `isAccessTokenId` never checks the grant shortcut: it reads the wrong offset and the condition is inverted.
findings.body: The grant shortcut sits at characters 4–5 of the prefix (`encodedContext.substring(4, 6)` in the decoder). The matcher instead takes `substring(3, 5)`, which for `onrtac` is `ta`. It then returns false when that value *equals* the expected shortcut. The two mistakes together mean that, in practice, any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` passes whatever the grant. The test assertions that replaced `isUUID()` therefore never verify the encoded grant type, and a wrong grant encoding would go unnoticed. Fix: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also check `items[0].length() == 6` first.

findings.title: New abstract `getShortcut()` breaks custom grant providers; the Javadoc's "3-letter" guidance produces IDs that can't be decoded, and a null shortcut breaks startup.
findings.body: The method is added with no default, so any existing custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, including test or extension grant factories not shown here, stops compiling. The Javadoc says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters". The decoder, though, requires the prefix to be exactly 6 characters, so it expects a 2-character grant shortcut. A grant that follows the doc gets 7-character prefixes, and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for every such token. A factory that returns null makes `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throw an NPE in `postInit`, which stops the server from starting. Fix: state and enforce the 2-character length when the maps are built in `postInit`, and consider a default implementation or a clear error message.

findings.title: The null check meant for `rawTokenId` checks `grantType` again.
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` a second time. A null `rawTokenId` is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` would then produce an ID like `onrtac:null`. Change the argument to `rawTokenId`.

held.title: Public copy constructor `Context(Context)` removed with no reason given in the request.
held.body: The change removes the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor. That is a public SPI type. Any caller that copies a context, such as extensions or other grant implementations not shown here, will no longer compile, and the request doesn't cover removing it. Also, `grantType` is only read once from `formParams` in the constructor. `setFormParams` doesn't refresh it, and a null `formParams` now causes an NPE here. Keep the copy constructor and have it copy `grantType`.
